-96.78500,32.79720.name: ReproMed Fertility Center
-96.78500,32.79720.desc: A fertility clinic reporting to the CDC's National ART Surveillance System. Medical director: Anil B. Pinto, MD. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. Reporting is required of every US clinic performing assisted reproduction, under the Fertility Clinic Success Rate and Certification Act, so this is close to a complete register rather than a list of members. What it records is cycles started, which is not the same as children born.

-79.96005,40.44096.name: Regional Biocontainment Laboratory (Center for Vaccine Research)
-79.96005,40.44096.state: 3501 Fifth Avenue Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania 15261, United States
-79.96005,40.44096.desc: A BSL3+ laboratory, operational. Run by Pittsburgh University. It is categorised as a university laboratory, working on animal health. It stands in a built-up area, with more than fifty thousand people living within two and a half miles. There is no international register of laboratories at this containment level and no obligation to declare one, so this record comes from a research project rather than a regulator. What that project could not find out is absent here too.

10.21000,56.15700.name: Cryos International
10.21000,56.15700.desc: One of the largest sperm banks in the world, shipping to more than a hundred countries from Denmark. Family limits are set per country and enforced per bank, so a donor can lawfully reach limits in a dozen jurisdictions at once and no one is counting the total. Donor-conceived people keep discovering sibling groups far larger than any published limit implies, and there is no register anywhere designed to prevent it. It sets no ceiling on children per donor because no international law sets one, states an aim of 25 to 50 families per donor, and has acknowledged that its donor exclusivity contracts are not very enforceable.

4.75000,52.69000.name: Bejo Zaden
4.75000,52.69000.desc: A Dutch vegetable breeder specialising in brassicas, carrots and onions, family owned and among the larger vegetable seed houses in the world. It works by conventional and marker-assisted breeding rather than transgenics, which is the norm in vegetables: the crops are too many, the markets too fragmented and the approval costs too high for engineered varieties to pay. Vegetable seed is where the concentration argument looks different from the commodity crops — a handful of European family firms rather than four multinationals.

112.93880,28.22820.name: Hunan Yuan Longping High-Tech Agriculture
112.93880,28.22820.desc: Named for the rice breeder whose hybrid varieties are credited with feeding a very large share of China, and now one of the country’s biggest seed companies. A reminder that the seed business in Asia grew out of public breeding programmes rather than out of chemistry companies. Yuan's work was conventional hybridisation done in a public institute and given away, which is the opposite of how the seed business now operates — and the company carrying his name is a commercial one. The contrast is the reason to record it.

-58.37600,-34.61100.name: CONABIA — Argentine biotechnology advisory commission
-58.37600,-34.61100.desc: Wrote Resolution 173/2015, which decided that an edited organism carrying no foreign DNA is not a GMO and needs no biosafety approval. Chile, Brazil, Colombia, Paraguay and Honduras all adopted versions of it, and the drafting was done here. More countries follow this text than follow any other on the subject. Its reach has since grown well beyond Latin America. Australia put SDN-1 edits outside the GMO definition in 2019; Japan required notification rather than approval on the same no-foreign-DNA test; England's Precision Breeding Act came into force in November 2025; New Zealand's bill, modelled on Australia's Act, was still before Parliament at the time of writing. The test each of them applies — could this have arisen naturally or by conventional breeding — is the one drafted here in 2015.
